newsitem.title: CUBA: French companies seek to boost investment in Cuba.
newsitem.headline: French companies seek to boost investment in Cuba.

text.p: French companies are seeking to boost investment in Cuba, and projects under negotiation include one by utility company Electricite de France to expand an existing Cuban power plant, a French trade mission said on Friday.

Jean-Pierre Desgeorges, deputy president of the French business association CNPF International, told a news conference that other planned projects included one by sugar trading firm Sucden to invest in modernizing a sugar refinery in eastern Cuba.

Desgeorges, who headed a week-long CNPF-organized trade mission to Cuba that ends on Saturday, detailed a series of planned projects in sectors including services, education, energy, food, industry and hotels.

He noted that France and Cuba are to sign an investment protection and promotion accord on April 25 in Paris, underlining the French government's interest in business ties with the island. Cuba has similar bilateral accords with nearly 20 countries.

Of the Electricite de France power project, Desgeorges said the plan under negotiation was to modernize and expand a thermal power plant at Santa Cruz del Norte east of Havana. This would be in conjunction with a Canadian firm that he did not name.

French Embassy sources said the electricity project would involve expansion to a total 650 megawatt capacity from the current 300 megawatt and would require investment of some $350 million to $400 million, with the investment recouped through sales of electricity to hard currency clients in industry.

Another French firm, Babcock, has been involved in modernizing two units of power plants in Santiago de Cuba and is discussing plans to continue this work in nine other Soviet-built units of power plants in Cuba.
Sucden's sugar refinery project would involve investment in the Juan Antonio Mella mill and refinery in the north of eastern Santiago de Cuba province.

Sucden has been one of a string of foreign trading houses and banks that have helped Cuba start recovering from a five-year slump in sugar cane production by providing credits toward input to the sector. Sucden has provided some $15 million worth of credits toward cane production in Santiago de Cuba province.
